population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: ever 17.6% − current 8.4% = 9.2% of adults used and are off now; ≈4.6 pts of current users (≈55%) are on a second or later course, and ≈2.8 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so 4.6+2.8 = 7.4 of 17.6 ever-users = 42% cycled. That is consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Current users ≈ 22.4M of ~267M adults. Age-band check: 18–29 (≈20% of adults) at 3.5, 30–49 (≈33%) at 7.5, 50–64 (≈24%) at 15, 65+ (≈23%) at 7 gives ≈8.4 overall. Income thirds (12.5/7.5/5.2) average to 8.4. Why current use fell 1.5 pts: (1) employer retreat. For 2030 plan years, coverage of obesity without diabetes, CVD or OSA codes fell from 58% to 47% of employers, and about 2.3M commercially covered users without a qualifying code were dropped. Roughly half moved to cash at $245–350 or $149 orals, and about 0.3M moved to imported pens. (2) Adherence-gated terminations in five Medicaid waiver states and under the new Medicare Bridge continuation rule. (3) Fracture-driven stops among women 65+ continue, but more slowly. (4) Prices are flat, so few new people start: ever-use rose only 1.1 pts. The middle third fell most, from 10 to 7.5, because it depends most on employer coverage. The top third holds at 12.5 on cash and concierge 'metabolic' regimens. The bottom third fell from 6.5 to 5.2: Medicaid gating terminations are partly offset by gray-market buying. Off-drug population: ≈24.6M adults used and are off now. Many of them are people whose coverage lapsed involuntarily and who regained weight; in waiver states a 12-month lockout keeps them off. ≈220M adults never used, mostly uninsured, bottom-third, or under 40. Pediatric: ≈0.35% of under-18s (≈255k), mostly adolescents 12+ on semaglutide under parents' diabetes-coded or cash coverage. The oldest adolescent users now have ~7 years of exposure, and no bone-accrual results have been reported yet. Gray-market users (≈1.6M) are counted as current but under-measured.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge renewed (Nov 2029) through Dec 2031 at an unchanged ~$245/month with a $50 copay and the same BMI/comorbidity entry criteria. New continuation rule: after 12 months, coverage continues only with ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and, for women 65+, a documented DEXA within 24 months. ≈1.4M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 1.4M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.1B/yr federal spend. Medicare overall (Part D diabetes plus Bridge) pays ≈21% of incretin fills ≈ 4.7M users (≈7% of ~63M adults 65+ ≈ 4.4M, plus ~0.3M disabled under-65 enrollees). Medicaid pays ≈10% of fills ≈ 2.2M users at $245: 2.2M × $245 × 12 ≈ $6.5B/yr gross before rebates, federal and state combined. Five states (Indiana, Arkansas, Ohio, Missouri, Oklahoma) run CMS-approved adherence-and-weigh-in waivers. Several others cover diabetes codes only.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 70+ generic semaglutide brands, $8–40/month. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 75–100/month. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China have generics. Generic oral semaglutide is available across ~170 countries. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices are stalled for a second straight cycle. TrumpRx/direct cash is still ~$245–350 for injectables and $149 for oral starting doses. Wegovy list is $1,349 and retatrutide list is $1,499; retatrutide still has no TrumpRx price and supply is still allocated, though less tightly. Manufacturers cite Section 232 tariffs, retatrutide capacity, and litigation over state Section 804 importation proposals. Payer mix of ~22.4M users: commercial 38% (8.5M), Medicare 21% (4.7M), Medicaid 10% (2.2M), cash/direct 24% (5.4M), gray/imported 7% (1.6M) = 100%. Commercial coverage is now mostly diabetes, established-CVD, OSA and CKD codes. About 55% of employers still covering obesity-only use adherence-gated PBM programmes (PDC ≥80% plus periodic verified weigh-ins), up from ~40%. Federal wellness rules still allow BMI-linked premium surcharges up to 30% of premium, and more employers that dropped coverage kept the surcharge. The result is two tiers: coded patients are covered and monitored, and everyone else pays $245–350 cash or buys Indian or Canadian pens by mail under the personal-importation gap. FDA and CBP seize parcels selectively and have prosecuted no individuals.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2028)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Dec 2026)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: smoking and vaping cessation: still off-label after the March 2029 complete response letter; prescribed via telehealth and some state quitlines
'metabolic health' / longevity use by people without obesity: low-dose oral semaglutide and Foundayo at $149 cash, concentrated in the top income third
alcohol reduction, including EAP referrals at the shrinking number of employers that still cover
pediatric under-12 use off-label under specialist care
reward/craving reduction for gambling and compulsive shopping, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached the US market in 2029–30. Survodutide (filed Oct 2027) received a complete response letter in Jan 2029 asking for body-composition and bone-density data in line with the class findings; Boehringer has not resubmitted. Amycretin (filed Jun 2028) received a complete response letter in Jun 2029 over manufacturing-site inspection findings at Novo's fill-finish plant; resubmission is expected in 2031. MariTide (monthly) completed phase 3 and Amgen filed in Sep 2030, so approval is no earlier than late 2031. Bimagrumab-based muscle-preserving combinations entered phase 3 in 2029 and are not on the market. Novo's semaglutide smoking-cessation sNDA got a CRL in Mar 2029: 12-month abstinence was not significant. The incretin market is ≈$102B in 2030, roughly flat. Lower US volume and ex-US generic erosion are offset by retatrutide's mix shift; Lilly gains share and Novo shrinks.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common class effect; still the leading cause of voluntary discontinuation, highest during retatrutide escalation.
Elevated with rapid weight loss, especially with ~28% loss agents and with repeated cycling.
No causal confirmation in long-term data; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; mass-tort litigation continues with no bellwether verdict yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Unchanged from 2028: roughly 1.5× sarcopenia criteria in 65+ users on therapy >2 years; lean-mass share of loss ~25–40%.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label (2028) recommendations stand; Medicare Bridge requires a documented counselling visit; survodutide CRL cites the class findings.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Follow-up cohorts hold hip/vertebral fragility fracture hazard ratios ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term users, concentrated in women and in cycling users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling stands; the Medicare Bridge continuation rule now requires DEXA for women 65+; Senate HELP issued its final report in 2029; the Novo DOJ civil matter settled without admission.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings-section mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in accumulating data.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The retatrutide postmarketing study using a validated anhedonia scale (SHAPS) found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~3% of treated participants vs ~2% on placebo at 52 weeks, dose-dependent. That is far lower than the 10–15% self-report surveys, and it fixes the effect as real but uncommon.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Added to Adverse Reactions for retatrutide and as a class mention for incretins (Apr 2030); no boxed warning. Many obesity clinics now include a short anhedonia screen at intake.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial regain within a year. Involuntary stops from employer retreat and gating terminations are now the largest source of discontinuation in the middle and bottom thirds.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: A federal district court (Feb 2030) largely upheld Indiana's waiver but required a 60-day notice before termination; CMS added the notice to all waivers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Observational signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein persist, especially in older and high-loss users and in unmonitored gray-market users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up now exist; cycling-and-bone question unresolved; pediatric bone-accrual studies enrolling, no results.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; FDA pediatric bone-accrual study requirement (2028) ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Compounded harms are rare after the 503B exclusion. Imported and counterfeit pen harms keep rising with the gray market; poison-centre calls about mail-order product are up again.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and selective parcel seizures; no individual prosecutions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent in real-world use; usually transient.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume pressure on snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks eases slightly as current users fall. Some 'portion-down' pack sizes are being quietly reversed in discount channels serving off-drug households, while premium channels keep protein, fibre and bone-health claims. Portfolios have split along the two access tiers.

alcohol.state: Heavy-drinker volume keeps contracting, but more slowly: EAP-referred use shrank as employers dropped coverage, and the cessation CRL removed an on-label tailwind. Spirits majors guide to flat-to-down volumes; tobacco 10-Ks still list GLP-1 off-label cessation use as a risk.

restaurants.state: Protein-forward small plates are permanent in affluent and office districts. Value chains in middle-income suburbs see some traffic recovery as off-drug customers return. The 'on/off' menu split is now standard.

apparel.state: Plus-size retailers are stable to slightly up as dropped users regain. Mainstream brands keep broad size runs; resale and alteration services do well among cyclers.

fitness.state: DEXA-plus-coaching chains and Medicare Advantage strength benefits keep growing on the Bridge counselling and DEXA rules. Mid-tier gyms see members leave when employer wellness budgets are cut.

insurance.state: Employers covering obesity-only use fell from 58% to 47%. The remaining coverage is concentrated on diabetes, CVD, OSA and CKD codes. Gating is spreading among those still covering (~55%). BMI surcharges outlive the coverage they were meant to support. Pharmacy trend has moderated to ~+5%.

pharma.state: The incretin market is flat at ≈$102B. Lilly gains through retatrutide and Foundayo; Novo shrinks after the scandal, the amycretin CRL and ex-US generic erosion. Survodutide's CRL chills glucagon-arm programmes, and deal flow concentrates on muscle-preserving adjuncts.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among insured, coded professionals over 40, being on the drug is unremarkable and being off is what has to be explained. The accepted explanations have narrowed to 'bone scan', 'pregnancy' and 'my plan dropped it'. The last now covers a whole stratum. Visible regain in middle-income workplaces reads as 'coverage', not character, and people say so out loud.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The gradient is stark: top third 12.5% against bottom third 5.2%. Local case: in Columbus, Ohio, the state's large health-system and insurance back offices dropped obesity-only coverage for 2030. Women 45–60 in billing and claims roles split three ways: those with a diabetes code stayed on, some pay $299 cash, and others went off and regained. In the same city, Ohio Medicaid enrollees schedule pharmacy-kiosk weigh-ins.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller shared meals, protein first and sweets as ceremony are still the norm among users. Holiday hosting still plans for 'on' and 'off' guests. In middle-income families the off guest is increasingly the one who lost coverage, not the one who opted out.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On/off' status on dating profiles is so common it is no longer interesting. Some users now add 'coded' or 'cash' as shorthand for stability. Mismatched appetites in couples are discussed openly and remain unquantified.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is still treated as something to manage medically. The new anhedonia line on the label lets users describe flatness as a recognised, uncommon side effect rather than a character flaw. People who regained after losing coverage are treated as people who were dropped, not people who failed.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. A validated postmarketing measure (SHAPS) finds clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~3% of treated vs ~2% of placebo participants at 52 weeks, dose-dependent; the labels now list it. Self-report surveys still show 10–15% 'less pleasure', which clinicians now read as mostly mild or confounded by weight-loss changes in eating and drinking.
interior_life.framing: An uncommon side effect, screened at intake and managed by lowering the dose. 'Steadiness' marketing to HR faded as employers dropped coverage and wellness vendors lost contracts. The cessation CRL took away the 'treatment' framing on-label, though off-label cessation prescribing continues.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Where coverage remains it is gated, and PBM adherence dashboards persist at ~55% of covering employers. Teamsters national freight contract language (2029) bars individual-level adherence data from reaching supervisors. DOT sleep-apnea screening still makes tirzepatide a practical requirement for many drivers, who now usually hold OSA codes. Middle-income office workers who lost coverage cycle off and back on with cash.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Writing off-dose' has become a dated joke. Musicians who mentioned drug holidays now cite 'the label'. High-stimulation leisure and 'one good drink' bars persist among users.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists and obesity clinics ask about dose and screen for anhedonia. Couples dealing with reduced desire now have a recognised cause and a standard step: try a dose reduction.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Cost and control dominate. The India/Canada price gap and the Colorado and Florida Section 804 import proposals are campaign material for 2030 midterm candidates in both parties. The Indiana waiver ruling and the Medicare continuation rule draw disability and senior advocacy groups together. There is no measurable effect on turnout or temperament.

state.regulatory_posture: Cautious. FDA issued complete response letters for survodutide, amycretin and the cessation sNDA, citing class bone/body-composition data, manufacturing and efficacy durability. It added the anhedonia labelling. Enforcement against imports is selective, and FDA has not ruled on the state Section 804 proposals.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Medicare Bridge renewed through 2031 at $245/$50. Medicaid coverage at $245 is state by state. TrumpRx cash prices frozen.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning has spread. Medicaid adherence-and-weigh-in waivers now run in Indiana, Arkansas, Ohio, Missouri and Oklahoma (≥80% PDC, quarterly verified weigh-in, a 12-month lockout after two misses, and a court-ordered 60-day notice). Medicare Bridge continuation beyond 12 months requires ≥80% PDC and DEXA for women 65+. About 55% of employers still covering obesity-only use PBM gating. BMI-linked wellness surcharges up to 30% of premium remain legal, including at employers that no longer cover the drug.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening is still a de facto tirzepatide requirement for some drivers, and the Teamsters data firewall limits employer visibility. The Army still allows GLP-1 use for recruits who meet accession standards; the policy is still contested.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs are still cited as the price floor. Colorado and Florida filed Section 804 proposals to import Canadian generic semaglutide, and Novo is suing. India–US trade talks list mail-order generics as an irritant. Retatrutide supply is still prioritised for the US market.

events.event: FDA issues a complete response letter for Boehringer's survodutide, requesting body-composition and bone-density data in light of the incretin class fracture findings; no resubmission date is set
FDA rejects Novo Nordisk's application to add smoking cessation to semaglutide's label after 12-month abstinence misses significance; telehealth clinics keep prescribing off-label

Benefits surveys show employers covering obesity-only GLP-1 use falling to 47% for 2030 plan years, with Ohio's largest health systems and several state employee plans restricting coverage to diabetes, cardiovascular, sleep-apnea and kidney codes
Colorado and Florida submit Section 804 proposals to import Canadian generic semaglutide; Novo sues, Lilly and Novo hold TrumpRx prices for 2030, and FDA has not ruled

CMS renews the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2031 at $245/$50 but makes coverage after 12 months conditional on 80% refill adherence and, for women over 65, a recent bone scan; Ohio, Missouri and Oklahoma Medicaid adherence waivers approved

FDA adds anhedonia to the adverse-reactions section of retatrutide and other incretin labels after a postmarketing study finds clinically meaningful loss of pleasure in about 3% of users versus 2% on placebo

open_tensions: Medicare and five Medicaid programmes now require continuous adherence to keep coverage, while the label warns that long-term and cycled use erodes older bones. The DEXA requirement monitors the harm that the adherence rule rewards.

Employers dropped the drug but kept BMI-linked surcharges. Middle-income workers who regained after losing coverage now pay a premium penalty for the regain, and no regulator has addressed the asymmetry.

Prices are stalled at $245–1,499 against $8–40 abroad. The Colorado and Florida Section 804 proposals and ~1.6M unmonitored gray-market users force an FDA decision the agency keeps deferring, and US exclusivity ends in 2031–32.

Anhedonia is now a labelled, uncommon side effect, but off-label cessation and alcohol prescribing still rely on the same mechanism. Adolescents on the drug since 2023 approach adulthood with no bone-accrual data.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Medicare pays ~$245 a month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay under the GLP-1 Bridge, on the same BMI/comorbidity entry criteria.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: Coded, Cash, or Off: The Weight Drug Is Normal Now. Keeping It Is the Hard Part.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about one American adult in twelve is on an incretin drug, down from one in ten two years ago. Nobody finds that surprising, and nobody finds the drug surprising either. In offices where people still have coverage, being on it is as unremarkable as wearing reading glasses. Being off it is what people ask about. The explanation has changed, though. A bone scan or a pregnancy used to be the usual answer. Now people mostly say their plan dropped it.

For 2030 plan years, fewer than half of employers still cover these drugs for obesity alone. The rest pay only when a claim carries a diabetes, heart, sleep-apnea or kidney diagnosis. The cuts fell hardest on the middle of the income distribution. Use in the top third is at about twelve and a half percent, held up by cash-pay and concierge 'metabolic' regimens. The middle third has dropped to seven and a half percent, and the bottom third to about five. In Columbus, Ohio, the large health systems and insurers that employ thousands of billing and claims workers restricted coverage to coded patients. A woman of fifty with a diabetes diagnosis kept her pen. Her deskmate without one either pays $299 a month or watches the weight return. Prices have not fallen at all. Injectables are still $245 to $350 cash, oral starting doses $149, and Wegovy still lists at $1,349. Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 with no discount channel. Lilly and Novo cite tariffs, capacity, and their lawsuits against Colorado and Florida, which want to import Canadian generics. Mail-order Indian pens keep arriving for the price of lunch. About 1.6 million Americans now use them, and no prescriber watches any of them.

The public programmes are generous on paper and strict in practice. Medicare renewed its $245 Bridge with the $50 copay through 2031. After the first year, a beneficiary now has to show eighty percent refill adherence, and women over sixty-five also need a recent bone scan. Indiana and Arkansas have been joined by Ohio, Missouri and Oklahoma in running Medicaid coverage through pharmacy-kiosk weigh-ins and refill audits. A federal judge largely upheld Indiana's version but ordered sixty days' notice before anyone is cut off. The arrangement rewards continuous use with one rule and monitors bone loss from continuous use with the next. Employers that dropped coverage mostly kept their BMI-linked premium surcharges.

Nothing new reached pharmacy shelves in these two years. The FDA sent back Boehringer's survodutide asking for bone data. It sent back Novo's amycretin over a factory inspection. It turned down semaglutide for smoking cessation because the effect did not last a year. Amgen filed its monthly shot in September, and it is a 2031 story at the earliest. The muscle-sparing add-ons everyone wants are in phase 3.

The one real change is in how people talk about flatness. A postmarketing study using a validated scale found that about three percent of users lose pleasure in a clinically meaningful way, against two percent on placebo. In April that went onto the label. The finding made the 'Ozempic personality' of 2026 smaller and more concrete. It is now an uncommon side effect, and a clinic intake form screens for it. When someone complains of feeling flat, the clinic lowers the dose. The HR language about 'steadiness' faded along with the wellness contracts. Truckers still take tirzepatide to pass sleep-apnea screening, but their new union contract bars refill data from reaching a supervisor.

Snack makers, restaurants and plus-size retailers have mostly adapted. Some have noticed that customers who lost coverage are coming back. Gyms that sell a DEXA scan with coaching keep opening, now on Medicare's referral. Seen from the street, nothing looks wrong. The access line now runs between people whose claims carry a diagnosis code and people who pay cash, buy imported pens, or go without.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Reyes weighs herself at 6:10 because it is Thursday, and Thursday is shot day. The vial came from LillyDirect, $299 on her own card since January, when the hospital system she codes claims for stopped covering anything without a diagnosis attached. She has no diagnosis. She has a number on the benefits portal, and it still carries a $41-a-paycheck surcharge.

At work, Tanya at the next desk eats half a turkey wrap and offers her the rest. Tanya has a diabetes code. Behind them, Greg has gained back the weight he lost and has stopped apologizing for it. Everyone knows it was his plan, not him.

At lunch Marisol texts her sister in Linden. Her sister's Ohio Medicaid kiosk weigh-in is due at the CVS by Saturday. She missed one in August. The letter said sixty days. She has the letter on the fridge.

In the afternoon she codes a DEXA scan for a seventy-one-year-old woman on Medicare. Medicare will keep paying for the drug as long as the scan is on file.

She gets home at six. Her son, fifteen, wants tacos. She makes three, eats one and feels nothing much about it. Last spring the clinic form asked her to rate whether she still enjoyed things she used to enjoy. She had circled 'agree' everywhere, a little surprised to mean it.

At 9:40 she pinches her thigh, counts to ten, and caps the syringe. On the counter is a pharmacy receipt for $299 and a flyer from her cousin: Indian pens, $38, shipped from Pune.
